promptText: Which hotel brands should an owner consider when evaluating branded residences as part of a hotel project globally?

payload.rawResponseText:
As of **August 2026**, an owner evaluating hotel-branded residences globally should consider a **targeted group of brands matched to the project’s positioning, location, buyer base and operating model**—not simply the most prestigious available name. Hotel brands still account for roughly 83% of existing branded-residence projects, although standalone residences are becoming increasingly common. ([knightfrank.com](https://www.knightfrank.com/research/article/2025-09-08-the-global-branded-residence-survey-2025))

## 1. Core global shortlist

| Project positioning | Brands that should generally be considered | Best suited to |
|---|---|---|
| **Trophy ultra-luxury** | **Four Seasons, Aman, Rosewood, Mandarin Oriental, Raffles, The Ritz-Carlton, Ritz-Carlton Reserve, St. Regis** | Prime gateway cities, trophy resorts, very high residential pricing |
| **Ultra-luxury resort** | **Aman, One&Only, Six Senses, Four Seasons, Rosewood, Ritz-Carlton Reserve, Montage** | Beach, island, mountain, golf and nature-led destinations |
| **Classic urban luxury** | **The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Waldorf Astoria, Raffles, Rosewood, Fairmont** | Mixed-use towers and prime city-center developments |
| **Contemporary luxury/lifestyle** | **EDITION, W, Pendry, Andaz, SLS, SO/, Mondrian, Delano, 1 Hotels** | Design-led urban projects with younger, internationally mobile buyers |
| **Luxury with broader market reach** | **JW Marriott, Conrad, Fairmont, Park Hyatt, InterContinental, Sofitel, The Luxury Collection, LXR** | Larger developments requiring strong distribution and somewhat broader buyer recognition |
| **Collection/independent character** | **Luxury Collection, Autograph Collection, LXR, MGallery, Emblems Collection, Vignette Collection** | Historic buildings or distinctive hotels where preserving local identity matters |
| **Asia-led resort and mixed-use** | **Banyan Tree, Capella, Shangri-La, Anantara, Kempinski, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood** | Southeast Asia, China, Indian Ocean and selected Middle Eastern destinations |
| **Regionally powerful alternatives** | **Address, Palace, Vida, Jumeirah, Fasano, Taj, Oberoi, Nikki Beach** | Markets where regional buyer recognition exceeds that of some global brands |

## 2. Highest-priority brands by category

### Established residential leaders

These should usually form the center of an international RFP:

- **Four Seasons** – One of the deepest dedicated residential operating platforms, suitable for integrated and standalone projects. Its current portfolio map covers dozens of properties across North America, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific. ([fourseasons.com](https://www.fourseasons.com/residences/private_residences/portfolio-map/))
- **The Ritz-Carlton / Ritz-Carlton Reserve** – Strong global recognition and an especially broad range of urban, resort and standalone applications.
- **St. Regis** – Particularly strong for formal, service-intensive luxury and urban trophy towers.
- **Mandarin Oriental** – Excellent for privacy-oriented urban luxury and select resorts; its operating and announced residential portfolio spans cities including London, New York, Bangkok, Barcelona, Vienna, Madrid, Muscat and others. ([mandarinoriental.com](https://www.mandarinoriental.com/en/residences))
- **Rosewood** – Strong “sense of place” proposition, suitable for intimate hotels, resorts and standalone residential projects. ([rosewoodhotels.com](https://www.rosewoodhotels.com/residences?utm_source=openai))
- **Raffles** – Appropriate for landmark, heritage and high-service projects, particularly in Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
- **Waldorf Astoria** – Strong combination of global recognition, Hilton distribution and formal luxury.
- **Aman** – Potentially exceptional pricing power and scarcity value, but only for extraordinary sites, architecture and development partners.
- **One&Only** – Particularly compelling for destination resorts, villas and second homes; its residential program includes rental management and homeowner exchange benefits. ([oneandonlyresorts.com](https://www.oneandonlyresorts.com/private-homes?utm_source=openai))
- **Six Senses** – A leading candidate where wellness, sustainability, nature and biophilic design are fundamental to the master plan rather than added amenities. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/a-natural-haven-on-portugals-blue-coast-six-senses-comporta-unveils-masterplan-for-new-resort-spa))

### Contemporary and lifestyle candidates

For projects targeting younger HNW buyers or seeking a stronger design, dining and social proposition:

- **EDITION**
- **W**
- **Pendry**
- **Andaz**
- **SLS**
- **SO/**
- **Mondrian**
- **Delano**
- **1 Hotels**
- **Kimpton**

Montage and Pendry are particularly residentially oriented: Montage positions residential as a primary driver of its business model, while Pendry translates art, music, dining and contemporary design into both hotel and residential products. ([montageinternational.com](https://www.montageinternational.com/development/))

### Broader luxury and larger-volume developments

For projects where ultra-luxury positioning would be difficult to support—or where a larger number of residences must be absorbed—consider:

- **Fairmont**
- **JW Marriott**
- **Conrad**
- **Park Hyatt**
- **InterContinental**
- **Sofitel**
- **The Luxury Collection**
- **LXR**
- **Westin**
- **Autograph Collection**
- **MGallery**

These brands can sometimes provide a better balance of residential pricing, construction standards, buyer awareness and ongoing service charges than an ultra-luxury flag.

## 3. Parent-company platforms worth approaching

### Marriott International

Marriott offers one of the broadest residential menus, with **16 residential brands**, including Ritz-Carlton, Ritz-Carlton Reserve, St. Regis, W, EDITION and Luxury Collection. This makes Marriott particularly useful when an owner wants to test several positioning levels through one development organization. ([marriottresidences.com](https://marriottresidences.com/brands/?utm_source=openai))

### Accor / Ennismore

Accor reports **25-plus residential brand offerings and more than 130 residential projects under development**. Relevant options range from Raffles and Fairmont to Sofitel, SLS, SO/, Mondrian, Delano and MGallery. Accor is worth considering for mixed-use, lifestyle and multi-brand developments, as well as projects outside the narrow ultra-luxury segment. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/hotel-development/solutions-for-every-project?mdrv=group.accor.com))

### Hilton

Hilton’s residential portfolio has expanded beyond Waldorf Astoria and Conrad to include LXR, NoMad, Signia, Curio Collection, Canopy and selected broader-market brands. Hilton reported 39 operating residential properties and 40 in development across 12 brands in its 2026 overview. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/whats-new-at-hilton-in-2026?utm_source=openai))

### IHG

The principal candidates are:

- **Six Senses** for wellness and destination resorts
- **Regent** for modern ultra-luxury
- **InterContinental** for internationally recognized urban luxury
- **Kimpton** for lifestyle projects
- **Vignette Collection** for independent or heritage assets

### Hyatt

The most relevant initial candidates are:

- **Park Hyatt**
- **Andaz**
- **Alila**
- **Thompson**
- Selected **Grand Hyatt** projects

Hyatt appointed a global head of branded residential in 2025, signaling a more coordinated residential growth strategy across its portfolio. ([investors.hyatt.com](https://investors.hyatt.com/news/investor-news/news-details/2025/Hyatt-Evolves-Brand-Portfolios-Continues-Growth-Momentum-with-Record-Pipeline-of-Approximately-138000-Rooms/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

## 4. Recommended RFP list by project type

### Prime urban hotel and residences

Invite approximately 8–10 of:

1. Four Seasons  
2. Ritz-Carlton  
3. St. Regis  
4. Mandarin Oriental  
5. Rosewood  
6. Raffles  
7. Waldorf Astoria  
8. EDITION or W  
9. Fairmont or Conrad  
10. One strong regional brand  

### Ultra-luxury destination resort

Invite:

1. Aman  
2. One&Only  
3. Six Senses  
4. Four Seasons  
5. Rosewood  
6. Ritz-Carlton Reserve  
7. Montage  
8. Banyan Tree  
9. Auberge Resorts Collection  
10. A strong regionally recognized resort operator  

### Lifestyle urban or resort project

Invite:

1. W  
2. EDITION  
3. Pendry  
4. Andaz  
5. SLS  
6. SO/  
7. Mondrian or Delano  
8. 1 Hotels  
9. Kimpton  
10. MGallery or Autograph Collection  

### Standalone residences without a hotel

Prioritize operators with demonstrated standalone capability:

- Four Seasons
- Ritz-Carlton
- St. Regis
- Mandarin Oriental
- Rosewood
- Raffles
- Waldorf Astoria
- W or EDITION
- Dorchester Collection
- Accor One Living brands

Standalone projects require particularly careful analysis of staffing, food and beverage delivery, homeowner charges and whether the brand can recreate its service proposition without hotel infrastructure. The proportion of pipeline hotel-branded residences co-located with a hotel is forecast to fall to about 70%, versus 82% of existing schemes. ([knightfrank.com](https://www.knightfrank.com/research/article/2025-09-08-the-global-branded-residence-survey-2025))

## 5. How the owner should select the winner

A suggested evaluation weighting is:

| Criterion | Indicative weighting |
|---|---:|
| Residential buyer recognition in target feeder markets | 20% |
| Evidence of achievable pricing and sales velocity | 15% |
| Residential operating and HOA-management capability | 15% |
| Hotel operating fit and expected hotel performance | 15% |
| Total fee burden and owner economics | 15% |
| Design standards and required development capex | 10% |
| Rental-program structure and legal feasibility | 5% |
| Contract flexibility, territorial protection and exit rights | 5% |

The evaluation should compare:

- Residential branding and licensing fees
- Technical-services and design-review fees
- Sales and marketing fees
- Ongoing residence-management fees
- Required FF&E and amenity standards
- Hotel–residence cost allocation
- Homeowner association governance
- Rental-pool requirements and owner-use restrictions
- Brand obligations after residential sell-out
- Brand-change and termination provisions
- Exclusivity radius and competing pipeline projects
- Whether services are delivered by the hotel, a separate residential team or third parties
- Expected annual service charges for buyers

## Bottom line

For most internationally marketed luxury hotel-and-residence projects, the **essential first-round shortlist** is:

**Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Raffles, Waldorf Astoria, Aman, One&Only and Six Senses**, supplemented by **W, EDITION, Fairmont, Conrad, Montage/Pendry, Banyan Tree** and one or two brands with particularly strong recognition in the project’s regional buyer markets.

The best brand is not necessarily the one promising the highest headline sales premium. It is the one whose **buyer recognition, design standards, fee structure, residential-management capability and service-charge burden produce the highest risk-adjusted total project value**.
